summary: Iteration 114 — full backend + frontend verification of the fix round: profile visibility, cards/drafts, notifications prefs + push gating (dedupe + ALWAYS_PUSH), remembered-accounts picker, account switch isolation, series highlights, AI summary gating, and password-reset token revocation. 14/14 backend pytest cases pass. All targeted frontend flows (account picker, picked-account requires password, multi-account persistence, Media tab tiles with Video badges on other user profile, series-highlights, OVC, forgot-password) verified. One minor security-hardening nit on password reset timing precision (see RCA).

minor.issue: tokens_valid_after is stored at the exact second of the reset. The validation uses `iat < int(valid_after.timestamp())`, where `iat` is JWT seconds. If a token was issued in the SAME second the reset occurs (rare but possible), the old token remains valid. With a >=1s gap old tokens correctly 401. Suggested fix: either compare `iat <= int(valid_after.timestamp())` or set `tokens_valid_after = now + timedelta(seconds=1)` in password_reset.py L84 and in revoke_all_user_tokens.

Returns 400 when the configured Resend/email provider is unreachable (preview env has no outbound SMTP for noreply@bruno.app). Only `send_email` raising HTTPException(500/502/503) is remapped to 503; other upstream HTTPException codes bubble up unchanged. Not blocking, but a 503 would be more accurate when email provider is misconfigured.

action_items: (Nice-to-have) Harden password reset timing: in /app/backend/routers/password_reset.py L84 use `datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=1)` for tokens_valid_after, OR change comparison in /app/backend/utils/security.py L106 to `iat <= int(valid_after.timestamp())`. Prevents the (extreme-edge) same-second window where an attacker's stolen token issued at the moment of password reset still authenticates for ≤1s.
(Nice-to-have) In password_reset.forgot_password, broaden the email-provider error catch so unavailable email returns a generic 200 (anti-enumeration) or an explicit 503 instead of leaking a 400.
critical_code_review_comments: push_notifications.push_allowed: correctly honors ALWAYS_PUSH={'account_security'} + 10-minute dedupe via db.push_log by tag. Dedupe does not fire for tag=='incoming_call' (intentional). Verified live.

GET /api/users/{user_id}/posts (posts_feed.py L1507): visibility filter now uses `{'$in': ['public', None]}` for non-followers and adds 'followers' when the viewer follows the owner. Correctly handles the 6 legacy posts in DB with no visibility field.

rememberedAccounts.js stores only {id,name,username,email,avatar_url,last_used} in encrypted secureStorage. Tokens are only stored on native (Capacitor). Verified: no plaintext password appears in DOM or any localStorage key (`Test1234!` string search returned 0 matches both in HTML and in localStorage dump).
AuthContext.clearPrivateCaches purges bruno_draft_*, bruno_outbox_*, bruno_autotranslate_* on login/account switch — correct per spec.

ViewCardPage.fetchCard sends Authorization bearer when a token is present — fixes 'Tarjeta no encontrada' for owner on fresh drafts. Verified: owner GET draft 200, viewer2 GET draft 403, anonymous 403.
SeriesHighlights returns null when list is empty — profile header is clean when the user has no series.

UserProfilePage media tab correctly renders a 3-col grid with thumbnails; videos get a 'Video' badge and tapping navigates to /reels?id=<postId> (observed 17 tiles for newtest viewed by viewer2, first tile has Video badge).
NotificationPreferences defaults: likes/comments/followers/messages/calls=False and order_updates/account_security/my_activity=True — matches spec exactly.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of in-scope flows (account picker, masked emails, no plaintext password in DOM/localStorage, remove account, 2-account persistence, pick→requires password, wrong-password error, Media tab tiles with Video badge, Series highlights, OVC branding, /forgot-password page)

rca of the issue: Password-reset token-revocation edge case: when reset_password() stores `tokens_valid_after = now_iso` (password_reset.py:84) using the same wall-clock second as a just-issued JWT's iat, the comparison in resolve_user_from_token (`iat < int(valid_after.timestamp())`) returns False because int() truncates sub-second precision, so iat == int(valid_after.ts). Steps to reproduce: (1) POST /api/auth/login (viewer2) → tok1; (2) within the same second, insert a password_reset_token row + POST /api/auth/reset-password → 200; (3) GET /api/auth/me with tok1 → 200 (should be 401). Mitigation: either compare with `iat <= int(valid_after.timestamp())` or shift `tokens_valid_after` by 1 second ahead. Verified: with time.sleep(3) between login and reset, old tok returns 401 as expected. Impact: extremely narrow race window; low exploitability but worth hardening.
